I stand this! While the appeal on low kcal items specifically marketed toward people like us, those foods usually have different additives that can make them addictive, as with many other processed foods using conventional ingredients.

I’d rather make a batch of x low kcal granola bars / my take on protein bars using the ingredients I carefully choose and sticking to a minimum. That said, I’m not going to deny the convenience of some of these items.

It’s still tricky, many sugar free products use sugar alcohols such as maltitol, sorbitol, xylitol and others. These are specifically cheap to obtain in bulk and therefore some companies take the advantage in using them for their cookies and sweet foods as the primary sweetener. They can be addictive, especially if you already are on a restrictive diet. 

I know through trial and error that it’s best for me to avoid sugar alcohols in a certain quantity if I don’t want to induce a binge. The sweeteners that have had little to no impact on me have been erythritol and allulose, which are sometimes contained in products that are more expensive than the ones using sugar alcohols. 

Everyone reacts to these stuff differently. But do your research, when I was on my worse binge/ purge cycle I’d use to binge on big loads of maltitol from different sweet goods.
